## Investment thesis
The downside case begins with a mismatch between capacity commitments and realized demand. This fictional counter-thesis tests the assumptions in the fundamental report.

## Business quality
Switching costs are useful only while the customer's platform remains in production. A new architecture could reset the competitive landscape.

## Valuation
Assume growth slows, operating margins contract, and working capital absorbs cash. No fair value can be estimated without an entry price, share count, and explicit discount-rate assumptions.

## Risks
- Customer spending may be cyclical rather than structural.
- Inventory commitments could remain after orders are deferred.
- Concentration magnifies the effect of one lost platform.

## Open questions
What evidence would distinguish a temporary pause from a structurally weaker business?
